claims.event: Reign years of this biography: Tianming 11 through Chongde 1. In Tiancong 8 Haoge followed him from Xuanfu toward Shuozhou and to Datong.
Took part in campaigns against the Dongkui, Chakhar, and Ordos, and was made a beile. In Tianming 11 he and Beile Daishan killed the Jarut beile Ezhaitu.
Defeated Ming forces at Jinzhou.
In the tenth month of the third year he joined someone whose name the text cuts off after 偕. He took the grain convoys at Tashan. A second-year episode is inserted before the narrative resumes.
With Jirhalang he attacked the Mongol Gutu tabunang, put him to death, and took his followers. The year numeral is 二年, written after the third-year sentence.

With Beile Manggu'ertai he scouted the Tongzhou ford, met Ning-Jin relief outside Guangqu Gate, and with Yuetuo and Sahalian besieged Yongping and took Xianghe. Dated to the third year resumed after the inserted second year.
Joined the campaign against Chakhar and raided the Guihua region. In the sixth month he was promoted to heshuo beile.

claims.statement: He advised taking Ming before Korea or Chakhar: not to stop at Jinzhou, to answer the border posts, rotate the army, and pincer Shanhaiguan from Ningyuan and the old road, or else hold Tongzhou.

claims.event: In the eighth month he raided the Shanhaiguan region.
Followed the emperor from Xuanfu toward Shuozhou. With Yangguli he broke the wall at Shangfang Fort, raided Shuozhou and Mount Wutai, and routed Ming relief at Datong.
With Dorgon he received Lindan Khan's son Eje, reached Tuolitu, and made an alliance. Returning, he raided Shanxi, broke Ningwu Pass, and entered Daizhou and Xinzhou.

label.en: Prince Su, in charge of the Board of Revenue

claims.event: Demoted to beile, removed from office, and fined a thousand taels for siding with Yuetuo in leaking a resentful memorial. He then joined Dorgon against Jinzhou while still overseeing the Board of Revenue, and entered Korea with him from Kuandian.
In the ninth month he lost the ministry and was fined a thousand taels because he did not punish Emoketu for trying to force Boluo's daughter on him.

Invaded through Dongjiakou, defeated Ming troops at Fengrun, took the surrender of Gaotang, raided to Caozhou, and captured Dongguang and Xian County. The year numeral is 三年, and Shunzhi 1 follows year 7, so this is Chongde 3. The name Haoge is not repeated until s0051.
On the army's return he was given two horses and ten thousand taels, resumed the Board of Revenue, and was restored to his former title. With Duoduo he defeated Ningyuan and killed Jin Guofeng.

With Dorgon he farmed at Yizhou, cut Jinzhou grain, and took platforms on the Xiaoling River. He beat off a night attack and engaged Hong Chengchou at Xingshan. He was then demoted to commandery prince for camping too far out.
Besieged Jinzhou again and defeated relief from Songshan and Shanhaiguan. Three of Chengchou's camps fell.

When the emperor planned to camp at Gaoqiao, Haoge asked to move between Songshan and Xingshan. He took Songshan by night after Xia Chengde's surrender, captured Chengchou and Qiu Minyang, and with Jirhalang took Tashan. He was restored and rewarded.
Lost his title after Heluohui reported remarks insulting Prince Rui. In the tenth month he was restored for service in the Central Plains, and that winter suppressed the Manjiadong bandits at Jining.
Marched west with Luolohun and Nikan. From Xi'an he sent Xingne to Binzhou and Dulei to Qingyang. Denglei, Guoxi, Kecheng, and Kede submitted, and Shaanxi was pacified.
Entered Sichuan in the eleventh month, sent Oboi ahead, and shot Zhang Xianzhong dead at Xichong. The eleventh month of Shunzhi 3 falls across AD 1646 and AD 1647.
By the eighth month of the fourth year the listed Sichuan districts were secured.
Returned and was feasted. Prince Rui then jailed him for covering a false claim of merit and for promoting Jisai.
Died in the third month, while still the prisoner of the previous sentence.
